Use the roadmap when you want to jump to another stage. Otherwise keep moving with the next and previous controls so the build stays in order.

Stage 1 Problem Specification Read the client problem as a real brief and turn it into a set of success criteria. 1 pages Stage 2 Planning and Database Design Move from interface planning into tables, fields, normalisation, relationships, and testing. 5 pages Stage 3 Build Foundations Set up the stack, learn the syntax families, and write schema.sql and init_db.py before the live features begin. 5 pages Stage 4 Feature Build Sequence Implement the project in a strict feature order, one controlled change at a time. 10 pages Stage 5 Non-Standard Algorithm Design the tagging logic in plain English before you attempt any code. 1 pages Stage 6 Database Extension Extend the data model for many-to-many tagging and verify that the design still holds. 1 pages
1 Planning documents Wireframes, screen planning, field mapping, and planning decisions. 2 Normalisation workshop Raw task data, 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, and field decisions. 3 Table planner Interactive table builder for fields, data types, keys, and example values. 4 ERD studio Interactive ERD builder with relationship mapping and diagram output. 5 Test plan Create a project test table before coding begins.

Start seeing the app before you build it

Use the wireframes to decide what belongs on screen, what belongs in the modal, and what can wait until later.

You are not decorating the app here. You are deciding what the first version must let the user see, click, and type.

Key words and definitions

TermMeaning
WireframeA simple planning sketch of the interface.
ModalA temporary form area used for focused input.
FilterA control that narrows which tasks are shown.
Field mappingMatching a screen control to a stored data value.

Wireframes

Planning notes

  • Decide where the user sees all current tasks.
  • Separate always-visible controls from controls that belong inside the add-task modal.
  • Agree how completed work will look different from active work.
  • Keep only the filters the brief can justify in version one.

Field mapping from the brief

FieldWhy it existsWhere it appears
TitleIdentifies the work itemTask card and add-task form
AssigneeShows responsibilityTask card, filter, add-task form
Due dateSupports urgency and planningTask card, sort/filter, add-task form
PriorityDistinguishes critical tasksTask card, filter, add-task form
StatusShows whether work is doneTask card and update action

What should be agreed before database design

  • The class has agreed which controls belong on the main page and which belong in the modal.
  • Every visible input in the wireframe maps to an identifiable data field.
  • The first version of the interface is clear enough to support database design.
